title: The Service Sector Is Back In Favor
text:
The Service Sector Is Back In Favor

Andrew Batson

Gavekal Dragonomics | 19 Aug 2026

The world’s manufacturing superpower has rediscovered the importance of services. From Xi Jinping on down, Chinese officials are now talking up services, from high-end research to low-end personal care, and issuing plans and targets to support the sector. That’s a notable shift after Xi spent the past several years reorienting China’s economy around the all-out pursuit of manufacturing supremacy. Xi’s focus on high technology as the key to achieving national greatness has certainly not wavered, but the execution of that strategy is adapting to current realities. The squeeze on manufacturing margins and the boom in artificial intelligence have helped convince the government that it needs to correct the excesses of the previous manufacturing drive.China’s government did not always disdain services. Under the leadership of Hu Jintao, government plans explicitly called for boosting the service sector’s share of GDP and employment. Some favoritism toward the service sector was seen as a necessary corrective to the industry-heavy economy China had inherited from the Maoist period. Top officials regularly discussed the expansion of the service sector as an important indicator of China’s progress toward becoming a developed economy and an advanced scientific and technological power.
